clue.text: Misplaced call to musician produces error

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the three words supply all fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets a phone call to a performer muddled and a blunder follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscalculation is a mistake in reckoning or judgement, so it is a kind of error.

clue.text: Work for Schubert perhaps making multiple copies

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: a staging of a sung Mass, the kind of choral work Schubert composed
the everyday meaning: manufacturing goods in huge identical quantities

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is being reproduced over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Schubert wrote several settings of the Mass, so a performance of one is literally a production of a Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory output of identical goods in vast numbers is the standard industrial sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Man blocks view in main route

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in the middle of it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to view is to see
a man's name

explanation.surface: A man stands in the way of the view along a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the poetic word for the open sea, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipping lane is a recognised route across the ocean, and the main is an old literary word for ocean.

clue.text: Plate served up with stout is dripping?

definitions.note: the question mark marks dripping as one example

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the word for plate is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer
stout means plump, fat

explanation.surface: A dinner plate carried in with a pint of stout, and someone asking if it is dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: Dripping is the British name for the fat that runs off roasting meat, kept for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is fat rendered from roast meat, so it is one example of fat from an animal.

clue.text: Charlie getting on man's nerves in wealthy district

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
belonging to a man
British slang: 'get on someone's wick' means get on their nerves

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie is irritating someone in a posh neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: CHISWICK is an affluent district of west London; the clue borrows the idiom 'get on someone's wick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiswick is a prosperous residential area of west London, known for expensive riverside housing.

clue.text: Checks borders

definitions.meaning: first meaning: restricts or restrains, as a verb
second meaning: boundaries or edges, as a plural noun

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests customs checks at a frontier; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means restrains or curbs; as a noun it means the outer edges or boundaries of an area.

clue.text: Have trying experience?

parts.note: surface reading: go through an ordeal, something difficult to endure
setter's reading: an experience of trying, that is sampling food or drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' sounds like 'stressful', but it means having a try, sampling a mouthful.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food or drink in small amounts is the verb sense of this word, an experience of trying flavours.

clue.text: Creditor showing explosive ego and bile

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: the letters of both words are combined as fodder

explanation.surface: A lender with a fiery temper and a bitter, self-important manner.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the party to whom an obligation such as a debt is owed is the one entitled to payment.

clue.text: Patriarch discovered during harvest grabbing female

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: discovered means found
during means in, as in 'in the night'
to harvest crops is to gather them
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: An old man is found out in the middle of harvest time, seizing a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the originator or senior figure of a family or institution, exactly the role of a founder.

clue.text: Angered animists taking line in totalitarian ideology

indicators.note: angry people are worked up and agitated, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Spirit-worshippers are furious at having to toe the party line under a dictatorship.
explanation.definitionFit: The system of rule associated with Stalin was a totalitarian doctrine of total state control.

clue.text: Organised discharge of colossal volume

indicators.note: 'of' here means drawn from, so the letters are taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A huge, deliberate outpouring, like a volley of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous, coordinated firing of guns is the standard military meaning of this word.

clue.text: Contrive to wipe out each unfinished city square

indicators.note: both of the preceding words are left incomplete, so each loses its final letter

parts.note: to contrive is to plan
to zap is to destroy or wipe out

explanation.surface: A scheme to demolish every half-built town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each' looks like part of the surface, but it tells you both words are cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish-derived word names an open public space or marketplace in a town.

clue.text: Looking ridiculous after carelessly consuming chocolate at Easter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for being embarrassed or made to look foolish

definitions.text: after carelessly consuming chocolate at Easter?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: smeared with a chocolate Easter egg after messy eating

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is taken literally: someone who has eaten a chocolate Easter egg sloppily would have it on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone humiliated after a mistake, appearing foolish in public.

clue.text: See 12
Arab sycophants shunning second one

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding or keeping away from, so the letter for second is left out

parts.note: yes-men are sycophantic followers
S is the abbreviation for second
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man from Arabia avoids a toady sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Conductor travelled to support those chosen

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter sits underneath, so the travel word goes below the chosen word

parts.note: the elect are those chosen
rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: An orchestra's conductor journeyed to back the selected few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a musician or bus worker, but here it is something that carries electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a solid electric conductor through which current enters or leaves a circuit.

clue.text: Single chap died embracing daughter as requested

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the single word wraps around the letter for daughter

parts.note: single means one
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a chap is a man
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A lone man dies hugging his daughter, as he had wished.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying something whenever it is asked for is the meaning of this phrase, as in video streaming.

clue.text: Attending Oxford maybe Ruth becomes arrogant

parts.note: being 'up' at a university means studying there; Oxford is one example
ruth is an old word for compassion or pity

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruth gets snooty once she is at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a name, but it is the old noun behind 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word describes someone self-important who behaves as if above their station.

clue.text: Crumpet and cooked leek in bread: no thanks

indicators.note: in places the mixed-up letters inside the word for bread
no means without, so the word for thanks is removed

parts.note: pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the vegetable's letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
TA is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A kitchen order: a crumpet plus cooked leek in a pitta, but don't bother thanking me.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion happens first: the bread loses its thanks before the vegetable goes inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a regional British name for a thin crumpet or griddle cake eaten toasted.

clue.text: Cook too little grub for starter and unfancied competitor

parts.note: to underdo food is to undercook it

indicators.note: a starter is the opening item, so only the first letter of grub is used

parts.note: the opening letter of grub

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: undercook the food for the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: The contestant whom nobody expects to win, the outsider in betting, is the classic sporting sense.

clue.text: Duke with healthier — though incorrectly formed — liver

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
a nonstandard comparative of well, meaning healthier; the setter admits it is not proper English

explanation.surface: A duke whose liver is in better shape, though the organ is malformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liver' reads as the organ, but it means one who lives somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A liver in the sense of someone who lives in a place is a resident or inhabitant.

clue.text: Scoundrel in American intelligence finds bug

indicators.note: in places the word for scoundrel inside the intelligence agency's initials

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rogue spy at the CIA discovers a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests a spy's microphone, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a loud chirping insect, and bug is a common word for an insect.

clue.text: Get lost on the moors?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rude command to go away
second meaning, read literally: go for a long walk across open upland

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like losing your way on a moor; the phrase is a dismissal and also literal walking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal slang ordering someone to go away, just as 'get lost' does.

clue.text: Man soon consumes ton

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the word for soon swallows the letter for ton

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
T is the abbreviation for ton

explanation.surface: A man will shortly eat a huge amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton is a male first name, and crosswords often define a name simply by its bearer.

clue.text: Leaders among the rabbinate examining food ascertain it to be so?

definitions.text: Leaders among the rabbinate examining food ascertain it to be so?

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Senior rabbis inspect a dish and declare it unfit under dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: rabbis examining food might declare it forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefa is food that is not kosher, which is what a rabbinical inspection would rule it to be.

clue.text: Initially obstructive wife to enable young head-turner

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of obstructive is used

parts.note: the opening letter of obstructive
W is the abbreviation for wife
to let is to allow or enable

explanation.surface: A difficult wife at first, who then gives in to a youngster turning heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head-turner' suggests someone attractive, but owls can swivel their heads almost all the way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby owl, a bird famous for rotating its head, is a young head-turner.

clue.text: Greeting Scottish banker and a regressively religious authority

indicators.note: regressing means going backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
a banker in crosswords is a river; the Tay is Scotland's longest river
taken as written

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a Scottish bank manager and a backward-looking cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a high-ranking Shia Muslim cleric and scholar in Iran.

clue.text: Outstanding leader — but one below par?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prominent leader of a movement or cause
second meaning, read literally: someone beneath a flag held aloft, a standard also meaning par

explanation.walkthrough: 'Below par' sounds like underperforming, but par is a standard, and whoever carries one stands beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who carries the flag at the front of a group is figuratively the leading champion of a cause.
